Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeZone on-prem: initial hardware + tenancy questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. We're getting ready to spin up our first customer-grade on-prem cluster for our ML inference workload. We wanted to capture a few constraints up front so Redwood can surface the best node placement and lifecycle guidance: 

- Multi-tenant model: 5 tenant namespaces initially, expected to grow to ~20 over 12 months.
- Workloads: mix of CPU control-plane + a fleet of GPU inference pods (A10G-equivalent), some batch preprocessing CPU jobs.
- Storage: local NVMe for model cache (fast ephemeral), + networked durable storage for snapshots / long-term artifacts.
- Networking: dual ToR, OSFP/BGP routing for east-west; traffic must be NATed for egress to our analytics cluster.
- Compliance: all tenant data must be encrypted at rest and we need auditable pod-level network allowlists.

Attached is a preliminary BOM and a rough placement sketch (edgezone-hw-bom.xlsx, placement-drawing-v2.png). Can you confirm Redwood's recommended node role split, eviction/taint policies for GPU nodes, and an approach for tenant-aware placement so noisy tenants don't affect others?

Also interested in your guidance for hot-swap capacity (how to provision spare nodes for GPU replacement without impacting SLAs).

Thanks,
Rajesh
Ops Lead, EdgeZone

Rajesh —

Thanks for the clear summary and attachments. Quick answers up-front and then a proposed agenda for a short workshop: 

1) Node role split: we recommend separate node pools for control-plane adjuncts (kube-proxy, operator pods), shared CPU workers (preproc + control), and dedicated GPU inference nodes. GPU nodes should be tainted (redwood.inference/gpu=true:NoSchedule) with tolerations on inference deployments.

2) Tenant-aware placement: use a combination of topologyConstraints + nodeSelectors and the Redwood pod-affinity scheduler plugin. Per-tenant ResourceQuota + PodTopologySpread will limit noisy neighbors. For stronger isolation, we can reserve a small dedicated GPU node pool for top-tier tenants.

3) Hot-swap: maintain a 10% spare GPU capacity cushion (idle nodes) in the autoscaling group and a documented node-replacement playbook (drain -> cordon -> reimage -> replace). We test rolling replacements in a canary window.

4) Storage: local NVMe for model cache (we suggest ephemeral PVCs with a local-storage CSI driver), and an NFS/MinIO-backed PVC class for durable snapshots, with encryption at rest via KMS.

I've attached a short Redwood on-prem checklist (redwood-onprem-checklist-v1.pdf) and proposed a 90-minute workshop to map tenant profiles to node classes. Proposed slots: Wed Aug 2 (10:00–11:30 PT) or Thu Aug 3 (14:00–15:30 PT). Let me know which works and we'll include Dev and Marcus for the hardware and networking bits.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: EdgeZone on-prem: initial hardware + tenancy questions

FYI — forwarding EdgeZone's initial ask. Short notes inline below.

>> Rajesh: multi-tenant model, NVMe + networked storage, BGP egress.

Our recommended high-level pattern (draft):
- Control plane: small dedicated supervisors + metrics nodes (3x m5-like), not scheduled for inference.
- Shared CPU workers: burstable for preprocessing (8–16 vCPU), use kubelet cpuManagerPolicy=static for predictable latency on latency-sensitive pods.
- GPU inference pool: A10G-class or equivalent, tainted. Two tiers: premium (dedicated for top 3 tenants) and standard (shared) with PodOverhead accounted for.
- Storage classes: local-ephemeral (CSI local), fast-network (NVMe over TCP or iSCSI), and archive (S3-compatible MinIO).
- Networking: Cilium with eBPF for L7 policies and NetworkPolicy enforcement, use hostPort for direct GPU device plugin traffic when necessary. For cluster egress, source-NAT at the ToR with per-tenant egress IPs (we'll need BGP prep).

Operational guidance:
- Node life-cycle: label with hw-serial, sku, and install-time image-id. Use rolling drain with PodDisruptionBudgets; for GPUs, prefer cordon+evict from the standard pool to the spare nodes.
- Monitoring: track per-tenant tail latency and model cache hit-rate; set auto-eviction thresholds (nodefs.available < 5%, memory.available < 10%).

I'll let Marcus/Dev validate the storage IO guidance below.

-K

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: EdgeZone on-prem: initial hardware + tenancy questions

Quick hardware mapping and practical notes: 

- GPU node sizing: 8x A10G per node (4x per host is more conservative depending on PCIe lanes); prefer 2x 64GB DDR + 4x 3.8TB NVMe for cache. Keep OS on separate SATA to avoid latency interference.
- Filesystem: ext4 for OS, XFS for NVMe model cache with noatime. Use fio profile from our benchmark suite (attached commands) to validate random read latency under load.
- Hot-swap: plan N+1 spares per rack for GPUs to avoid cross-rack traffic in replacement. Use a small pool of pre-provisioned images and an automated reimage job (images signed and pulled from the private registry).
- CSI: recommend local-static-provisioner for local-ephemeral (fast, simple) and Rook-Ceph for durable block if customers want replication. If they prefer managed NFS, ensure the NFS appliance supports lock recovery during node drains.

Action item: I'll provide an fio deck and a node-replacement Ansible playbook by Wed EOD so EdgeZone can smoke test disk behavior.

- Dev

- Replacement drill: perform a single GPU node drain/replace with failover to spare nodes; < 5 minutes of degraded tail latency.
